clue.text: Female and I meet at bar, not long before clock strikes

parts.note: to bar something is to veto it, forbid it

explanation.surface: A woman arranges to meet someone at a pub just before the hour chimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a pub, but it is the verb meaning to forbid; 'meet at' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A time such as five minutes short of the hour is just before a clock chimes the hour.

clue.text: Swimmer drinking coffee that's mostly rather dull

indicators.note: the swimmer drinking something means the swimmer's letters hold that drink inside

parts.note: a fish is a creature that swims

indicators.note: mostly means the word for the coffee loses its last letter

parts.note: a latte is a milky espresso coffee

explanation.surface: A fish sipping a coffee seems a bit of a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' signals a container: the swimmer holds the coffee, and 'mostly' drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not very exciting or lively is somewhat flat in tone, which is what the suffix -ish softens.

clue.text: Writer volunteers to get stuck into new version of oliver!

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means going inside it, so these letters are put within the others
a new version of a word reworks its letters into a fresh order

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's force of volunteer reservists

explanation.surface: Some volunteers help stage a fresh production of the musical Oliver!
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the musical's title; 'new version of' makes VOLIRE, and 'to get stuck into' puts the Territorial Army inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Enlightenment philosopher wrote Candide and many other works, so he is a famous author.

clue.text: Nice surprise for nurse

definitions.meaning: an unexpected pleasure laid on for someone
to nurse a patient is to give them medical care, a verb sense

explanation.surface: A carer gets an unexpected bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant unexpected gift is a delight, and a doctor or carer gives a patient medical care.

clue.text: White wine and assortment of pates the French stocked

indicators.note: a shop stocked with something holds it inside, so these letters take another word within
an assortment mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: A deli counter with various pâtés sells a white wine too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pates' here is pâtés, the meat spread; 'assortment of' makes SPATE, which 'stocked' fills with the French plural article.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a German late-harvest wine, usually sweet and white, made from grapes picked late.

clue.text: After trial, striker X appears in important M fixture

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'After trial, striker X appears in important M fixture': stray 'X' and 'M' are OCR noise, so the printed wording is unknown; TEST + MATCH is clear but the clue cannot be quoted honestly.

clue.text: Wild animals from parts of Asia?

parts.note: Asia is the East, and E is the abbreviation for east
parts of the world are lands, regions or countries

explanation.surface: A question about where certain wild beasts come from in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild animals from parts of Asia?' suggests creatures native to Asia, but these antelopes are African; the question mark admits the pun of 'East lands'.
explanation.definitionFit: These large African antelopes live in the wild on savannah grassland.

clue.text: Team can be accommodated in hotel eventually

indicators.note: being accommodated in a hotel means being lodged inside it, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A whole sports side can eventually be put up at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, so the number stands for the side.

clue.text: One making friends, as it were, in part of the Auvergne

definitions.text: One making friends, as it were
definitions.meaning: someone who allies themselves with others, a jokey invented noun
a French department and river in the Auvergne region of central France

explanation.surface: Someone sociable finds friends in a corner of central France.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who forms alliances, and also a French département and river in the Auvergne.

clue.text: Where plane flies and exhibits speed

parts.note: to air something is to display it, so airs means exhibits
pace is rate of movement, speed

explanation.surface: A plane flies around and shows off how fast it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibits' looks like a noun, but it is a verb, AIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky above a territory, controlled by its state, is the region an aircraft travels through.

clue.text: Wearing casual clothes for lecture

definitions.meaning: choosing informal wear rather than smart dress
a lecture here is a severe scolding, a telling-off

explanation.surface: Someone in jeans and a sweatshirt gives a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing informal clothes is one sense; a stern reprimand is the other.

clue.text: Pastry dish rejected by politician speaking out at a restaurant

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so these letters run in reverse order

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish with a filling

indicators.note: speaking out means what follows is a sound heard, not a spelling

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: An outspoken politician sends back a tart at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TART into TRAT; 'speaking out' gives TORI, which sounds like TORY, a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian eatery serving simple food is a kind of informal restaurant.

clue.text: Mosquito-like insect returning, say, at dark

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters of the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means when it introduces an instance
dim means dark, lacking light

explanation.surface: A biting insect comes back as the light fades.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny biting fly resembles a small mosquito and swarms in summer.

clue.text: Computer programmes showing what chambermaid must do

definitions.meaning: software in which data sits in rows and columns of cells
a hotel maid lays out bed linen when making up a room

explanation.surface: Software described as a hotel maid's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Data tables in software like Excel are one sense; laying linen on a bed is the other.

clue.text: Great figure the result of this technique?

definitions.text: Great figure the result of this technique?

parts.words: Great figure the result of this technique?
parts.note: a joke linking a conqueror called 'the Great' with a posture method named after the same name, as if the method produced the man

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a great man was made by a method.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king was called the Great, and the posture-training method is named after F. M. Alexander.

clue.text: American dealt with privately

indicators.note: something dealt with is sorted or handled, so the letters are reshuffled like a dealt hand

explanation.surface: An American was handled in private.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin legal phrase for a hearing held in a judge's chambers, away from the public, so in secret.

clue.text: Live male creature, a monster

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
he is the male pronoun
a moth is a creature, a flying insect

explanation.surface: A living male creature turns out to be a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creature' is vague; here it is a MOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant beast in the Book of Job is now any huge or monstrous thing.

clue.text: Requirement for émigré?

parts.note: the letters of the word regime, rearranged, spell émigré, so a change to regime gives the clue word

explanation.surface: Asking what someone who has emigrated needs.
explanation.walkthrough: An émigré may have fled because a new government was needed; cryptically, REGIME with its letters changed spells EMIGRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppling a government is what an exile hopes for; also an anagram instruction for the word regime.

clue.text: Successful player and composer?

definitions.meaning: a player who gets a goal or points
someone who writes musical scores, a jokey sense marked by the question mark

explanation.surface: A good player also writes music.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal-getter in football is one sense; a person who writes a musical score is the other.

clue.text: Card game is quiet, unusually quiet

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A card game that is strangely silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'quiet' is the musical marking piano; 'unusually' makes IQUET from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old two-player card game played with a 32-card pack.

clue.text: Powerful country's machinations seen from within

indicators.note: seen from within means looked at from the inside, so the letters lie inside this word

explanation.surface: A superpower's plotting is viewed by an insider.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asian nation is a world superpower.

clue.text: Good friend joins one outside trendy boozer?

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so these letters go round another word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
an ace is a one in cards
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A good friend joins someone outside a trendy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' is British slang for a pub; a gin palace was a gaudy Victorian bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy Victorian public house is a type of bar, which British slang calls a boozer.

clue.text: A challenge, they say, for legendary firefighter

indicators.note: they say means as it is spoken, so a sound is heard here

parts.note: a dare is a challenge

explanation.surface: A challenge for a famous oil-well firefighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Adair was a famous American who put out oil-well fires.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Red Adair fought oil-field fires, which made him a legend.

clue.text: Suddenly attacks plump lad

parts.note: round means plump or chubby
a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly attacks a plump boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone abruptly in anger is to assail them without warning.

clue.text: Manage to organise party

parts.note: to make a plan is to organise it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Coping by throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by with what you have is to cope or manage.

clue.text: Stopping work when repeatedly getting weary?

parts.note: re- means again, so it stands for repeatedly
tiring means getting weary

explanation.surface: Quitting your job because you keep growing tired.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies giving up work from exhaustion; RE + TIRING is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's job for good at the end of a career is what a pensioner does.

clue.text: Tribute given by top BBC man during broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard over the air, so this is a word as said aloud

parts.note: Lord Reith was the first director-general of the BBC

explanation.surface: A former BBC boss gives a tribute on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Reith is said 'reeth', matching the sound of the funeral tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers laid at a grave or memorial honours the dead.
